keyboard.action: Into the menubar: focus the first item on first entry, afterwards optionally the item that last had focus, else the first enabled item. From an item: leave the menubar and close all menus.
As Tab, in the reverse direction of the page sequence.
Move focus to the next menubar item, optionally wrapping from last to first.
Move focus to the previous menubar item, optionally wrapping from first to last.
On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item.
On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its last item.
On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item. Otherwise activate the item.
As Enter; on a menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio, change its state.
Move focus to the first menubar item.
Move focus to the last menubar item.
Move focus to the next item in the current menubar or menu whose label starts with the character.
With focus in the bar after a context action opened it: optionally return focus to the invoking context.
On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item. Otherwise activate the item and close the menu.

On a menuitemcheckbox: toggle it without closing. On an unchecked menuitemradio: check it and uncheck the others of its group without closing. On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item. On any other item: activate it and close the menu.
Move focus to the next item, optionally wrapping from last to first.
Move focus to the previous item, optionally wrapping from first to last.

On an item with a submenu: open it and focus its first item. On an item without one: close the submenu and all parent menus, move focus to the next menubar item and, if that item has a submenu, open it (recommended: without moving focus into it).

In a submenu of a menu item: close the submenu and return focus to its parent item. In a submenu of a menubar item: close it, move focus to the previous menubar item and, if that item has a submenu, open it (recommended: without moving focus into it).
Move focus to the first item of the current menu.
Move focus to the last item of the current menu.
Move focus to the next item of the current menu whose label starts with the character.
Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to what opened it (menu button, parent item, or invoking context).
Move focus out of the menu to the next element in the page sequence and close all menus and submenus. Tab never moves focus into a menu.
Move focus out of the menu to the previous element in the page sequence and close all menus and submenus.

focus.entry: Tab focuses the first item the first time and optionally the last-focused item afterwards.
focus.exit: Tab or Shift+Tab leaves and closes every open menu.
focus.restore: Escape in a menu returns focus to the menubar item that opened it.
focus.note: When moving along the bar from an open menu, the next item's menu opens but focus stays on the bar item (recommended).

variants: navigation menubar (items that both navigate and open)

keysNotBound.reason: Named as the Windows command that opens a context menu; see context-menu.
An example of an application shortcut that focuses a menubar from an editor; not a binding of the pattern.

rtlDecisions.question: In a horizontal roving-focus composite (tabs, toolbar, menubar, radio group, toggle group), which arrow moves to the next item in RTL?
rtlDecisions.apg: Silent, apart from one aside in the tabs page that calls the last tab the right-most "in a left-to-right horizontal tab list". Keys are named physically: Right Arrow is next.

libraries.behaviour: ArrowLeft is next in RTL for tabs, toolbar and horizontal radio groups; vertical arrows never flip.
The composite root swaps the forward and backward horizontal keys when direction is rtl.
The roving focus group swaps ArrowLeft and ArrowRight before mapping a key to a focus intent when dir is rtl; toggle group, tabs, toolbar, radio group and menubar all pass dir through it.
Tabs and ToggleButtonGroup pass isRtl to the roving tabindex root.
Tabs flip the arrow offset when rtl and the tab bar is top or bottom; a horizontal menu maps Left to next when rtl.

rtlDecisions.reason: Items are laid out from inline-start, so the arrow that points at the visually following item must move to it. All five libraries agree.

rtlDecisions.question: Which arrow opens a submenu from a vertical menu, and which closes it, in RTL?
rtlDecisions.apg: Silent. No pattern page mentions right-to-left; keys are described physically (left, right) for a left-to-right layout. Right Arrow opens a submenu, Left Arrow closes it.

libraries.behaviour: In RTL ArrowLeft opens the submenu and ArrowRight closes it.
SUB_OPEN_KEYS and SUB_CLOSE_KEYS are keyed by direction: rtl opens with ArrowLeft, closes with ArrowRight.
List navigation takes an rtl flag; the cross-orientation open and close keys are ArrowLeft and ArrowRight respectively when rtl.
In a vertical menu Left means "children" (open) and Right means "parent" (close) when rtl.

rtlDecisions.reason: A submenu opens toward inline-end, which is the left in RTL; the arrow must point where the submenu appears.

data.notes: RTL: the bar starts at the right, so ArrowLeft is next; inside menus ArrowLeft opens a submenu, or on a leaf item moves to the next bar item, and ArrowRight closes a submenu or moves to the previous bar item. In a vertical menubar with horizontal menus the arrow pairs exchange roles. For an item that both navigates and opens a submenu, Enter and Space navigate and ArrowDown opens.
